rule: ENSURE: When computing AOV from integer-like aggregates, verify whether SQLite integer division is expected before forcing float math | CONTEXT: In this case, SUM(total_payment) / COUNT(order_id) matched gold behavior better than SUM(...) * 1.0 / COUNT(...) | WHEN_TO_CHECK: Any per-group average where numerator and denominator come from integer-valued aggregates | EXAMPLE_USAGE: Compare both formulations and keep the one matching expected output semantics.

VERIFY: Output numeric type/precision matches evaluation expectations (integer-like vs decimal) | PRINCIPLE: Correct logic can still fail if output type/precision differs from target | WHEN_TO_APPLY: Any aggregate expression that may return float by default | EXAMPLE_USAGE: If expected values are integer-like, avoid unnecessary float promotion and apply explicit casting only when required.

ENSURE: For year-span components in SQLite date arithmetic, prefer STRFTIME-based component extraction over julianday/365 approximations | CONTEXT: julianday-based decomposition introduced drift in career-span computations | WHEN_TO_CHECK: Date interval decomposition into year/month/day parts | EXAMPLE_USAGE: Use ABS(CAST(strftime('%Y', end) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', start) AS INTEGER)) for the year component.

ENSURE: For fractional months, use month-component subtraction divided by 12.0 rather than julianday modulo heuristics | CONTEXT: (julianday diff % 365)/30.44 can misalign calendar month boundaries | WHEN_TO_CHECK: Converting month differences into fractional years | EXAMPLE_USAGE: Use ABS(CAST(strftime('%m', end) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%m', start) AS INTEGER)) / 12.0.

VERIFY: Calendar-aware date parts (year/month/day extraction) are preferred over average-day approximations when exact component semantics matter | PRINCIPLE: Average-day approximations introduce drift in boundary-sensitive calculations | WHEN_TO_APPLY: Date decomposition tasks and tenure/career-span style metrics | EXAMPLE_USAGE: Favor extracted components over raw day-count decomposition.

ENSURE: Fractional-year formulas are internally consistent across components (year + month/12 + day/365) | PRINCIPLE: Mixing exact and approximate components can bias final averages | WHEN_TO_APPLY: Composite duration formulas | EXAMPLE_USAGE: Keep all component calculations aligned to the same calendar model.

ENSURE: When segmenting collisions by helmet usage, first restrict to cases with motorcycle-related safety-equipment evidence using EXISTS against parties | CONTEXT: Without this filter, unrelated cases contaminate helmet_not_used aggregates | WHEN_TO_CHECK: Collision-level classification derived from party-level attributes | EXAMPLE_USAGE: Add EXISTS (...) with party_safety_equipment LIKE '%motorcycle%' before computing helmet buckets.

VERIFY: If category assignment depends on a related table, enforce membership with EXISTS (or equivalent) before aggregation | PRINCIPLE: Aggregating before relational eligibility checks causes denominator pollution | WHEN_TO_APPLY: Any classification using attributes from a secondary table | EXAMPLE_USAGE: Apply eligibility EXISTS first, then compute category rates.

ENSURE: In order-level payment analyses joined to item-level tables, deduplicate order-payment pairs before counting category-level totals | CONTEXT: One-to-many joins (orders -> items) can inflate payment counts if counted post-join | WHEN_TO_CHECK: Metrics that are logically order-level but computed after joining item-level records | EXAMPLE_USAGE: Build a DISTINCT order_id/payment_type/category relation in a CTE before GROUP BY.

ENSURE: Monthly net-balance logic must subtract both withdrawal and purchase txn types (not withdrawal alone) | CONTEXT: Omitting purchase undercounts outflows and shifts month-level balance comparisons | WHEN_TO_CHECK: Net balance formulas from mixed inflow/outflow transaction logs | EXAMPLE_USAGE: CASE WHEN txn_type='deposit' THEN +amt WHEN txn_type IN ('withdrawal','purchase') THEN -amt END.

ENSURE: For complete customer-month summaries, materialize full customer x month keys, LEFT JOIN transactions, and COALESCE aggregates | CONTEXT: Direct GROUP BY on fact rows drops zero-activity months and biases downstream extremes | WHEN_TO_CHECK: Time-series summaries where missing periods must appear explicitly | EXAMPLE_USAGE: Generate month keys, CROSS JOIN customers, LEFT JOIN facts, then COALESCE(SUM(...),0).

ENSURE: Split added-to-cart events into purchased-vs-abandoned using visit-level EXISTS/NOT EXISTS purchase checks, not constants | CONTEXT: Hard-coded zeros or raw event_type counts miss the visit-level conversion condition | WHEN_TO_CHECK: Funnel splits where one event's status depends on whether a later event occurred in the same visit/session | EXAMPLE_USAGE: SUM(CASE WHEN add_to_cart AND EXISTS(purchase in same visit) THEN 1 END) and corresponding NOT EXISTS branch.

ENSURE: Use normalized date keys (e.g., parsed YYYYMMDD integer/date) for previous-row lookups and ordering, not raw string dates | CONTEXT: Lexicographic date ordering can select wrong previous rows and corrupt daily-change metrics | WHEN_TO_CHECK: Correlated subqueries or window logic for previous/next date records | EXAMPLE_USAGE: Compare/order on parsed_date consistently in both predicates and ORDER BY.

ENSURE: Duration bucket CASE thresholds must use the same unit as the source column and match intended boundaries exactly | CONTEXT: The source duration is in milliseconds; threshold unit mistakes silently misbucket rows | WHEN_TO_CHECK: Rule-based bucketization of numeric measurements | EXAMPLE_USAGE: Define short/medium/long using millisecond boundaries if the column is Milliseconds.

VERIFY: If category ranges are policy-defined, output boundary labels from rule constants rather than observed MIN/MAX per bucket | PRINCIPLE: Data-driven MIN/MAX describes sample extremes, not canonical bucket limits | WHEN_TO_APPLY: Reporting from/to labels for fixed-threshold categories | EXAMPLE_USAGE: Emit range labels via CASE on category constants while revenue remains aggregate over joined facts.

ENSURE: Exclude ensemble 'Stack' rows and compute best traditional model per (name,version,step) before counting L1_model frequency | CONTEXT: Counting all rows mixes candidate models and overstates category frequency | WHEN_TO_CHECK: 'Most frequent best model' style metrics | EXAMPLE_USAGE: Filter model <> 'Stack', select top score per partition, then aggregate winners.

VERIFY: Use only validated key relationships in joins; avoid extra predicates (like step) unless proven part of the key relation for the target metric | PRINCIPLE: Overconstrained joins can drop valid winner rows and distort aggregate counts | WHEN_TO_APPLY: Enrichment joins after top-per-group selection | EXAMPLE_USAGE: Join on the minimal validated key set required by the metric's grain.
